name: Uruguay
summary: Uruguay taxes residents' foreign interest and dividends at 12% and, since 1 January 2026, also foreign capital gains (12% of the gain, or an elective 2.4% of sale price). New residents from 2026 can opt for an 11-year holiday on foreign capital income if they spend 183 days a year or make a qualifying investment (USD 2m real estate or about USD 100k a year in funds). There is no inheritance tax (3% ITP on inherited Uruguayan real estate) and a 0.1% wealth tax on Uruguayan assets only.

regimes.name: Ordinary tax residence
regimes.description: Residents pay IRPF at a flat 12% on capital income, including foreign interest and dividends and, from 1 Jan 2026 (Law 20.446), foreign capital gains and foreign rents. Dividends from Uruguayan companies 7%. Net wealth tax at 0.1% on Uruguay-located net assets above about UYU 6.65m.
regimes.eligibility: Resident if 183+ days, or centre of vital/economic interests in Uruguay (spouse and minor children living in Uruguay create a presumption), or qualifying Uruguayan investments.

capital_gains.summary: From 1 Jan 2026, gains on foreign movable assets (e.g. foreign shares) and foreign real estate are taxable at 12% of the actual gain; the taxpayer may instead elect a deemed gain of 20% of the sale price (2.4% of price) or 15% for real estate (1.8%). Gains on Uruguayan shares 12%; titles issued by Uruguayan entities effectively 2.4%.

capital_gains.rate_basis: 12% IRPF capital income rate on actual gain (Deloitte 2026; PwC reviewed 2 Sep 2026). The annual election of a deemed 20%-of-price base (effective 2.4% of proceeds) can be far cheaper for large gains. Listed foreign assets bought before 2026: cost stepped up to the 31 Dec 2025 quoted value (Galante & Martins).
capital_gains.important_exceptions: Real estate transfer tax (ITP) 2% each for buyer and seller on Uruguayan property.
capital_gains.foreign_assets: Taxed from 2026 (previously foreign gains were outside IRPF). Transparency rules for 5%+ stakes in foreign entities introduced by the May 2026 decree.
open_questions: Implementing decree of 6 May 2026 not read in the original; withholding mechanics (possible 8% final rate via local agents) still pending as of April 2026.

dividends.summary: Foreign dividends and interest: 12% IRPF, with credit for foreign tax up to the Uruguayan tax. Dividends from Uruguayan companies: 7% withheld.

dividends.rate_basis: Deloitte 2026: 7% on dividends from resident companies, 12% general rate for other capital income; credit for foreign tax on foreign investment income.
dividends.withholding_outbound: 7% on dividends to non-residents (from 2026 also where profits were untaxed under IRAE, if the recipient's country taxes them and grants a credit).
dividends.treaty_network: About 25 treaties; BEPS MLI in force since 1 Jun 2020. No comprehensive US treaty.

wealth_tax.summary: Impuesto al Patrimonio: residents pay 0.1% on net wealth located in Uruguay above the non-taxable minimum (UYU 6,653,000 per person; double for a family unit). Foreign assets are outside the base.

components.name: Impuesto al Patrimonio (personas físicas)
components.notes: PwC (2 Sep 2026): residents 0.1%, threshold about USD 160,000 for 2026. The UYU 6,653,000 figure comes from Forvis Mazars and a calculator site; whether it is a deductible allowance or only a filing threshold should be confirmed. Real estate valued at cadastral value.

wealth_tax.property_tax_note: Municipal real estate tax (contribución inmobiliaria) applies separately.
open_questions: Conflict: PwC/calculator give a single 0.1% resident rate; another source describes progressive 0.1%-1.6% bands being phased down. 0.1% used.

inheritance.summary: No inheritance or gift tax. Inheritances of Uruguayan real estate bear the property transfer tax (ITP) at 3% of cadastral value for children (4% for other heirs).

sources.title: Deloitte International Tax: Uruguay Highlights 2026
DGI: Trasmisión causa muerte, heredero hijo natural - tasa aplicable (ITP)

inheritance.gift_tax: No gift tax; gifts of Uruguayan real estate also attract ITP.
inheritance.important_exceptions: ITP 3% (children) applies to Uruguayan real estate only, on cadastral value; a foreign portfolio passes free. children_treatment taxed_low reflects ITP on local real estate.
open_questions: ITP rate for inheritances confirmed only by a 2006 DGI publication.

regimes.name: Tax holiday for new residents (Law 20.446, from 2026)
regimes.description: Individuals becoming tax resident from 1 Jan 2026 may elect to be taxed under IRNR (non-resident tax, territorial) on foreign capital income and gains for the year of arrival plus 10 years. Foreign dividends, interest and gains are then untaxed. The former permanent 7% option is not available to 2026 arrivals.
regimes.eligibility: New tax residence from 2026. If residence is via 183 days' presence: no investment needed, presence must be kept each year. If via centre of interests or investments: real estate over UI 12,500,000 (about USD 2m) or annual fund capitalisation of UI 625,000 (about USD 100,000) in productive/research projects.

capital_gains.summary: Foreign gains not taxed during the holiday; Uruguayan-source gains taxed as usual.

capital_gains.rate_basis: Election to apply IRNR on foreign-source capital income for 1+10 years (Galante & Martins; Forvis Mazars). private_business_sale 0.12 assumes a Uruguayan company; a foreign company stake would be 0.
open_questions: Implementing decree details for the investment routes.

The consolidated text of the new-resident holiday as amended by Law 20.446 was not located on IMPO in this pass (the law's IMPO page lists article 653 amending T.O. 2023 Title 7 art. 6, which brings foreign capital income and gains into IRPF from 2026, and article 193 amending Title 8 art. 10); the 1+10-year IRNR option and the end of the permanent 7% option rest on Galante & Martins and Forvis Mazars.

dividends.summary: Foreign dividends and interest not taxed during the holiday; Uruguayan dividends 7%.

residency.tax_residency_test: 183+ days (sporadic absences count), or base of activities/vital or economic interests in Uruguay, or presumptions based on investment (e.g. UI 3.5m real estate from 1 Jul 2020 plus 60 days' presence; UI 15m in companies with 15 jobs) (PwC reviewed 2 Sep 2026).

routes.name: Legal residence (temporary/permanent)
routes.requirements: Residence permit via Dirección Nacional de Migración; tax residence via presence or investment as above. Amounts for migration not researched.

prime_rent_monthly.description: Median monthly asking rent of the 20 four-bedroom houses listed for rent in Carrasco (Montevideo's most expensive district) on InfoCasas on 15 Oct 2026; range USD 3,300-12,000, most USD 4,200-6,000 for 250-450 m2 houses, often with pool. One listing in UYU excluded.

source.title: InfoCasas: casas en alquiler, Carrasco (Montevideo), 4 dormitorios

prime_price_per_m2.description: Carrasco average residential price per m2, mid-2025, from an El Observador report cited by Global Property Guide. Punta del Este frontline luxury apartments (Mouette, Trump Tower) quoted at USD 7,000-10,000/m2 by the same page.

source.title: Global Property Guide: Uruguay residential property market analysis (price history)

cost_of_living.notes: International school fee not sourced: the Uruguayan American School (Montevideo) does not publish fees on its website or brochure; no other school fee page was opened. Health insurance and housekeeper not sourced. Rents are quoted in USD.

us_citizen_notes: US citizens remain subject to US federal income, estate and gift tax on worldwide income and assets; the app adds the federal layer. Local tax can generally be credited against US tax on the same foreign-source income only where the US foreign tax credit rules allow.
open_questions: Law 20.446 implementing decree (6 May 2026) details on the holiday investment routes and post-holiday options (50% rate for 5 years; fixed annual payment of UI 1,875,000 for 20 years) not read in the original.
Residents who opted for the old regime before 2026 (including the permanent 7% option) keep it; not modelled.
